description:
The shared result comparator silently widens equivalence in two engine-justified
but globally-applied ways, each of which can mask a real cross-surface value
divergence:
  - validation.py:718 (_numeric_values_equal) treats float('nan') and None as
    both "missing" and reports two missing values as EQUAL. Combined with
    _normalize_value mapping NaN->None, a DataFrame surface that produces a
    spurious NaN (e.g. 0/0 from a division bug) compares EQUAL to a SQL NULL.
  - validation.py:693 strips leading/trailing whitespace unconditionally
    (val1.strip() == val2.strip()), so "foo " vs "foo" is declared equal - masking
    a real transcription difference.
Both are justified for specific engine decode paths (e.g. ClickHouse Arrow/pandas
NULL decode, CHAR padding) but are applied engine-agnostically with no flag to
disable, so they widen equivalence for every gate.

Make both behaviors explicit comparator flags (e.g. treat_nan_as_null,
strip_strings) that default to STRICT, enabled only where an engine genuinely
needs them and documented at that call site.

anti_patterns.why: a value oracle that equates NaN with NULL or ignores trailing spaces by default cannot be trusted to catch those bug classes.

preserves.behavior: Engine decode paths that genuinely need NaN-as-null or CHAR-padding tolerance still pass, via the explicit opt-in flag at that site.
Float relative-tolerance (1e-10) comparison semantics are unchanged.

prior_art.concept: {'ref': 'benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py / dataframe_surface.py (_normalize_value)', 'note': 'Where NaN->None normalization happens; enable the widening flags only where a specific engine decode requires it.'}
{'ref': 'benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py:693', 'note': 'Unconditional string .strip() compare - add a strip_strings flag, default False.'}
{'ref': 'benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py:718', 'note': '_numeric_values_equal NaN/None handling - add a treat_nan_as_null flag, default False (strict).'}

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/equivalence -q && make ssb-cross-surface-equivalence-report
verifications.description: Strict default catches widened divergences; enforced gates stay green
verifications.expected: new strict-default tests pass; all enforced gates still 0 divergent

work_units.notes:
Add treat_nan_as_null and strip_strings flags (additive, default False so the
strict behavior is the default). Thread them through the comparator entry
points. Enable them ONLY at the specific engine decode sites that genuinely
need them, with an inline comment justifying each. Keep TPC-Havoc and all
enforced gates green (verify none silently depended on the widening - if one
does, that is a divergence to surface, not to preserve).
work_units.summary: Gate NaN==NULL and whitespace-strip behind comparator flags, default strict

work_units.notes:
Unit tests asserting, under the strict default: a DataFrame-side 0/0->NaN vs
SQL NULL is CAUGHT, and "foo " vs "foo" is CAUGHT. And that the opt-in flags,
where set, still accept the engine-justified case.
work_units.summary: Test that the strict default catches the masked divergences
